name: ABL proto-oncogene 2, non-receptor tyrosine kinase
pathways: negative regulation of Rho protein signal transduction

function.text: ABL2 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase ABL2. Annotated molecular activities include protein kinase activity and protein tyrosine kinase activity. It participates in signal transduction and negative regulation of Rho protein signal transduction.

germline.text: No constitutional disease assertion was retrieved in the reviewed GenCC snapshot; this does not exclude a germline association.

somatic.text: ABL2 can participate in leukemia-associated rearrangements, including fusion with ETV6. Interpretation requires the actual fusion structure and disease context.

function.text: ABL2 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase ABL2. Based in part on similarity, it is a non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that plays an ABL1-overlapping role in key processes linked to cell growth and survival such as cytoskeleton remodeling in response to extracellular stimuli, cell motility and adhesion and receptor endocytosis. It binds directly F-actin and regulates actin cytoskeletal structure through its F-actin-bundling activity. It participates in the regulation of cell adhesion and motility through phosphorylation of key regulators of these processes such as CRK, CRKL, DOK1 or ARHGAP35.
